statement.p: Use Stokes' Theorem to find the circulation of the vector field \vec{F} = 2xz\vec{i}+(x+yz)\vec{j}+3x^{2}\vec{k} around the paths. C, is the circle x^2+y^2 = 4, z=1, oriented counterclockwise when viewed from above.

static.solution: \int_C \vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r} which can be evaluated directly by parameterizing the circle, C. Or, since C is the boundary of a flat disk S, we can use Stokes' Theorem: \int_C \vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r} = \int_S \mbox{curl }\vec{F} \cdot d\vec{A} where S is the disk x^2+y^2 \le 4, z=1 and is oriented upward (using the right hand rule). Then \mbox{curl }\vec{F} = -y\vec{i} + 4 x\vec{j}+\vec{k} and the unit normal to S is \vec{k}. So \int_S \mbox{curl }\vec{F} \cdot d\vec{A} =\int_S (-y\vec{i} + 4 x\vec{j}+\vec{k}) \cdot \vec{k} \, dx dy = \int_S 1 \, dx dy = 4\pi.
